overview: White supports e4 with f3 for a Sämisch-style set-up and avoids the main Pirc theory. After 3...g6 4.c4 Bg7 5.Nc3 O-O 6.Be3 it resembles a King's Indian Sämisch, with Black striking at the centre with ...e5 or ...c5. 3...e5 is the other main branch.

white_ideas.idea: Build a solid centre with c4, Nc3 and Be3, then Qd2 and kingside play.
Use the space and consider castling queenside for a pawn storm.

black_ideas.idea: Fianchetto and castle quickly, with counterplay on the queenside.

typical_structures.structure: King's Indian Sämisch-like chain with ...e5 against d4/f3/e4.

character.notes: Opposite-side castling and counter-strikes are common; White has space but a loosened kingside.

structure.notes: Centre tension; may become closed after d5 and ...e5 or open after dxe5.

approach.notes: A rare anti-Pirc idea from White, seldom chosen by strong players.

level.notes: Like the Sämisch KID: clear ideas but needs feel.

sublines_that_differ.name: Queenswap
sublines_that_differ.how: An early queen trade for a quiet position.

character.reason: Sämisch-style play with opposite-side castling and counterstrikes.

structure.reason: Centre could close or open depending on ...e5.

plans.reason: White's central space against Black's breaks.
